title: Portfolio report
context: Admin report listing every user's total portfolio value. Production has about 2 million users with about 15 positions each.

refs.title: Java and databases: an overview (Marco Behler)

points.title: N+1 queries
points.why: One query loads the users, then one more query per user loads their positions: about 2 million queries.
points.fix: Use JOIN FETCH or @EntityGraph, or better, a single aggregate query.

points.title: Loads every user into memory
points.why: 2 million users plus 30 million positions as entities will exhaust the heap.
points.fix: Paginate or stream (Slice, keyset pagination, or a Stream with a fetch size).

points.title: Aggregation done in application code
points.why: Summing in the app moves every position row over the network when the database could return one row per user.
points.fix: SELECT user_id, SUM(market_value) … GROUP BY user_id into a projection.

points.title: EAGER on a collection
points.why: Every query that loads a User also loads all their positions, even when they aren't needed.
points.fix: Use LAZY (the default for @OneToMany) and fetch explicitly where needed.

points.title: Foreign key needs an index
points.why: Looking up positions by user_id without an index is a full table scan per user.
points.fix: Add an index on positions.user_id in a migration.
